```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A has a sourced proof that a single operator can reach meaningful revenue in this exact category: Instatus at about $10k MRR (starterstory). B offers no comparable solo-operator revenue proof point. Its 'already being rebuilt by solo developers' claim points to Upstep, a free open-source tool, not a paying business.",
    "A's pricing-pain evidence is specific and sourced. Statuspage's split public, private and audience billing runs from $399 to $1,499+/mo, which leaves a $9–$29 entrant a concrete price gap to sell into within 90 days. B's main price complaint says even $50–80/mo is 'ridiculous', which signals resistance to paying at all rather than a gap to undercut.",
    "Both categories are saturated with free tiers: OneUptime in A; Canny, Featul, Upstep and the 50% free-plan rate in the 62-tool study in B. B's own brief adds a marketer's warning that generic feedback tools get ignored. So B's saturation looks at least as severe and is more thoroughly documented.",
    "A's product scope (incidents, components, subscriber emails, public page) is narrower and has a clear moment of urgency (an outage). That favors a fast first sale for an agent-run solo company. B's scope (widget, roadmap, voting, changelog) is broader and more discretionary.",
    "B's acquisition evidence is weak and partly generic. The Google Ads CPC figure is an all-industries average, and the Product Hunt data is a single anecdote. A's channel evidence is also modest, but it includes a category-relevant observation: Hyperping is already running the SEO wedge."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's main demand quote about scattered bug reports comes from an indie builder promoting their own feedback widget. It shows a builder's motivation, not a prospective buyer's willingness to pay. B's other demand quote shows price resistance at $50–80/mo, which undercuts the brief's claim that willingness to pay at $25–$79 is proven.",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence. Both briefs describe crowded, commoditized categories with free incumbents, and neither has direct evidence that a new entrant can land a first paying customer within 90 days. A wins mainly on its solo-revenue proof point and sharper pricing pain, not on a decisive difference in evidence quality. A's own biggest risk, selling against OneUptime's free tier, is unresolved."
}
```
